title: Logitech G102 (G203) LIGHTSYNC: Is This Budget Gaming Mouse Still Worth It?
summary: The Logitech G102 LIGHTSYNC — sold as the G203 LIGHTSYNC in the US and Europe — is a light, wired, six-button gaming mouse with RGB lighting and a 200–8,000 DPI sensor. Here is who it suits, what it lacks and what to buy instead.
description:
## Who is it for?

- Players who want a simple, light wired mouse for FPS and MOBA games.
- First-time PC gamers on a tight budget.
- Students and office users who want one mouse for work and play.

## Why consider it?

- Logitech lists a 200–8,000 DPI sensor and a 1,000 Hz report rate.
- Around 85 g, with a compact symmetrical shape.
- LIGHTSYNC RGB and G HUB software for buttons, DPI steps and lighting.

sections.title: G102 or G203? Same mouse, two names
sections.content:
Logitech sells this mouse under two names. In the US, UK and Europe it is the G203 LIGHTSYNC; in much of Asia and some other markets it is the G102 LIGHTSYNC. Logitech's own G102 product page even uses G203 in its description and images. If you shop on Amazon US, UK or Germany, search for "G203 LIGHTSYNC" — that is the name the links on this page use.

Don't confuse it with the older G102/G203 Prodigy, which has a different lighting system. Check that the listing says LIGHTSYNC.

sections.title: Design and grip
sections.content:
Logitech lists the mouse at 85 g (without cable) and 116.6 × 62.15 × 38.2 mm. That is a compact, symmetrical shape that suits claw and fingertip grips and medium-to-small hands. People with large hands who palm their mouse may find it short.

The side buttons sit on the left only, so it is not a true ambidextrous mouse for left-handed players.

sections.title: Sensor and performance
sections.content:
According to Logitech, the sensor covers 200–8,000 DPI and the mouse reports at 1,000 Hz (1 ms). Most players use 400–1,600 DPI, so the top of that range matters less than consistent tracking. Logitech does not publish a sensor model name for this mouse, and we have not measured it ourselves.

For competitive FPS players who want the lowest weight or wireless freedom, there are lighter and more advanced options (see Alternatives).

sections.title: Software, RGB and onboard memory
sections.content: Logitech G HUB lets you remap the six buttons, set DPI steps and program LIGHTSYNC RGB with about 16.8 million colors. Logitech says you can program up to five presets. Its spec listings also mention onboard memory, but descriptions differ between regional pages, so if carrying settings between PCs without G HUB matters to you, confirm it on your local Logitech page.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't
sections.content:
Buy it if you want an inexpensive, light wired mouse from a major brand with easy software. It is a safe first gaming mouse.

Skip it if you want wireless, a mouse under 60 g, a large ergonomic shape for palm grip, or a published switch-lifespan rating. Logitech's product pages don't list a click rating; some retailer listings quote 10 million clicks, but we couldn't confirm that with Logitech, so we don't rely on it.

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used this mouse in person. This is a research roundup based on Logitech's US and regional product pages and spec listings (checked November 2026); see the Sources list at the end of this review. Images are official Logitech product photos.

sections.title: Should you buy the Logitech G102 / G203 LIGHTSYNC?
sections.content: Yes, if your budget is tight and you want a wired mouse that just works. Its strengths are a light 85 g body, sensible software and a price that is often below its US$39.99 list price. If you can spend a little more, a wireless or lighter mouse will feel more modern — compare the alternatives below before you buy.

pros: Light 85 g body (Logitech spec) that is easy to move quickly.
200–8,000 DPI range and 1,000 Hz report rate listed by Logitech.
Six programmable buttons and up to five presets in G HUB.
LIGHTSYNC RGB is easy to customise and sync with other Logitech gear.
Compact symmetrical shape suits claw and fingertip grips.
Widely available worldwide under the G203 or G102 name.
cons: Wired only — no 2.4 GHz or Bluetooth option.
Side buttons on the left only; not suited to left-handed players.
Short body may feel small for large hands with a palm grip.
Logitech doesn't publish a sensor model or click-lifespan rating.
Two regional names (G102/G203) plus an older Prodigy version can confuse buyers.

faq.question: Is the Logitech G102 the same as the G203?
faq.answer: Yes. Logitech sells the same LIGHTSYNC mouse as the G203 in the US, UK and Europe and as the G102 in much of Asia. Make sure the listing says LIGHTSYNC, not the older Prodigy.

faq.question: What DPI does the G102 / G203 support?
faq.answer: Logitech lists an adjustable range of 200–8,000 DPI, set through Logitech G HUB.

faq.question: Is it wireless?
faq.answer: No. It is a wired USB mouse with a 2.1 m cable, according to Logitech. For a wireless option at a similar budget, look at the VXE R1 SE or the Logitech G305.

faq.question: Is it good for FPS games like Valorant and CS2?
faq.answer: It is a capable budget option thanks to its light weight and 1,000 Hz report rate. Competitive players chasing the lowest weight may prefer an ultralight mouse such as the VXE R1 SE (about 51 g).

faq.question: What warranty does it have?
faq.answer: It depends on where you buy. Logitech offers a limited hardware warranty whose length varies by region, so check your local retailer or Logitech's regional site.

faq.question: Does it work on Mac?
faq.answer: Logitech G HUB is available for Windows and macOS. The mouse itself works as a standard USB mouse without software.

verdict_summary: A light, simple wired gaming mouse from a major brand. It lacks wireless and a published durability rating, but remains a sensible budget pick if you want something that just works.
